subject: Production Private VPC - intermittent decode errors & throughput drop
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@orsonmed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Dorn <alex.dorn@orsonmed.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden latency + decode errors in our private cluster

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and intermittent decode errors on our private VPC cluster starting ~11:30 PST. Several of our nightly job runs failed and a subset of live requests returned 5xx decode errors (stack trace attached by our infra team). Throughput capacity also dropped by ~30% according to our internal telemetry.

This is impacting Orson's triage and billing pipeline; we have a scheduled billing run at 02:00 and are nervous about missed windows. Can Redwood confirm if anything changed on your end (model variant, runtime config, or kernel updates) and advise an immediate mitigation?

Short timeline:
- 11:30: increased p95 and occasional 502 decode errors
- 11:40: consumer-backpressure, request queue growth on the private pool
- 12:05: some jobs requeued, but failures continued for ~20% of requests

We need an RCA and, if possible, a temporary mitigation (routing, rollback, config) that doesn't require downtime.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen
Head of Platform
Orson Medical

Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + decode errors in our private cluster

Lydia — thanks for the heads-up and very sorry you're seeing this. We're prioritizing this now. Immediate plan:

1) I'm spinning up a dedicated diagnostics session against your VPC instance (no code changes) to capture KV cache metrics, kernel scheduling, and queue length.
2) Marcus/Vivek/Priyom: please gather recent kv cache eviction counts, decode error logs, and per-host CPU/GPU utilization. Attach any traces to this thread.
3) Lydia: can you confirm whether you rolled any config or model pins in the last 48 hours?

If we need a temporary mitigation, we'll propose either a short canary revert to the last-known-good model variant (fast) or a temporary autoscale/burst increase on the dedicated pool (requires your approval for the burst window).

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + decode errors in our private cluster

Quick triage notes (prelim):
- Observed elevated KV cache miss and eviction rates on Orson's private pool starting ~11:25 PST. Eviction rate spike correlates with p95 increase.
- Several hosts show kernel-level stalls during token decoding (stack traces attached). The stalls align with larger sequences from a small subset of requests (long-form documents).
- GPU utilization hasn't dropped overall; instead, tail latency increases appear tied to thread contention on the decode path and high L2 cache pressure.

Attached: kv_evictions_snapshot_20261219.json (KV metrics dump), perf-traces-12-19-20.zip (perf samples).

Prelim mitigations to propose:
A) Increase max-kv-cache-size for the pool to reduce evictions (config-only, no deploy). Low risk, immediate effect if memory headroom exists.
B) Apply a soft limit on sequence length at the routing layer for live traffic to protect the hot path (short-term, affects a minority of requests).
C) If evictions persist, temporarily route a percentage of production traffic to a warmed standby model variant with a slightly different KV mapping (requires brief prep).

I'll keep digging into host-level traces.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@orsonmed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency + decode errors in our private cluster

Lydia — quick note from Solutions / runtime side. We can implement A+B from Marcus in ~10–20 minutes provided Orson is comfortable with a brief configuration change and a conservative sequence-length soft cap (we can set the soft cap at the 99th percentile to avoid customer-visible regressions).

If you'd like us to take the autoscale/burst route instead, we'll need authorization for a single 60-minute elevated capacity window (billing as agreed in the MSA). That would be safer if you prefer to avoid any request shaping.

Naomi: if Orson approves config tweak + soft cap, Priyom and I will coordinate the change and run a fast verification (smoke) across the pool. We'll post traces to the Drive link and update HubSpot ORS-4582.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
